tweets: Chandrayaan-1 lifts off from Sriharikota on 22 October 2008, India's first voyage to the Moon. Carried by a PSLV-C11 rocket built entirely at home, it bore eleven instruments — five Indian, the rest from Europe and the US — into orbit around another world.

Weeks later, its onboard Moon Mineralogy Mapper detected water molecules in lunar soil — evidence confirmed in 2009, reshaping what we know about the Moon. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history.
